Nigeria · Contact

Talk to us about your right of way in Nigeria

Tell us about the line, route or site and what the record is for. We reply by email with the questions we need answered, and then with a written proposal covering the scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

About you
About the route or site

What do you need?

Location or province, the buffer distances to check, and any date the record must reflect.

Your request reaches us through FormSubmit, a form-delivery service. Read the privacy notice.

What happens next

  1. We reply by email to confirm what we need from you.
  2. A short scoping call about the route or site, the distances that matter and the imagery.
  3. A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

What to send

The route or boundary file (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the country and province, the distances to check, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables you need and your deadline. No file yet? Describe the location and we can draw the route with you.

Procurement teams

Send your supplier or prequalification forms, or the tender documents, with your request. The proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

For a route or site in Nigeria

  • The states and LGAs the line or site crosses, so we can check the imagery that exists for the area.
  • The asset: crude, gas or product pipeline (and the licence strip as a polygon, if you have it), or a power line and its voltage.
  • The widths to report: the NESIS right of way for the voltage, the distance in any Oil Pipelines Act s.12 order, or your company or lender standard.
  • Satellite only, or drone detail too. Drone surveys need NCAA and ONSA authorisations and, near high-tension lines, a special authorisation, so the proposal shows their lead time. See drone law in Nigeria.
  • The date the record must reflect, such as a cut-off date, a handover date or the date a line was built.
  • Who should receive the results, so they go only to the contacts you name.
  • For upstream oil and gas work: whether the contract needs NOGIC JQS registration, an NUPRC service permit or an NCDMB-approved Nigerian content plan, so the proposal can address each one.
  • For mini-grid site work: the candidate communities or sites, as points or boundaries, and the household assumptions your programme uses, if any.

Frequently asked questions

Do you need a site visit or a drone flight to start?

No. A survey in Nigeria starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or imagery you already hold, so nobody travels and no aircraft flies. Drone detail is added only where a stretch needs it, subject to the NCAA and ONSA authorisations each job requires.

Can we send a route through an insecure area?

Yes. Satellite work needs no one on site. The route and the results go only to the contacts you name, military and other sensitive sites are masked, and we never publish maps of your assets or of the settlements around them without your written permission.

Which date can the register reflect?

The date the imagery was captured. For a cut-off date, a handover or the date a line was built, we look for dated scenes close to that date and tell you what exists before you commit. A new capture can be requested when the archive is too old; its date depends on satellite availability and weather.

Our security department sets rules for any work on the line. Can you follow them?

Yes. Tell us who in your security or asset-protection team should be involved. Satellite work involves no one on site; any drone flight near a flow station, terminal, substation or military site is planned through your security department, with the owner’s written consent, and sensitive sites are masked in the deliverables.

Can we send tender or prequalification documents?

Yes. Send the documents with your request, and tell us the portal, the prequalification category and the Nigerian content requirements your process uses. Our Nigerian content and procurement notes set out the registrations a Nigerian buyer usually asks about.

We have no route file yet. Can we still ask?

Yes. Describe the line, the states and LGAs it crosses, or send tower or kilometre-post coordinates, and we draw the route with you and send it back for your confirmation before any survey runs.
